main_text.p: dium : nempe intolerabilem fastum ac superbiam, præ- sertim diuitum mercatorum. Postea subijcit amplisi- mam consolationē, in qua etiam tempus præsinit (post septuaginta uidelicet annos) quo ea denuò ad pristi- nam redibit dignitatem : & non solum ingentes recu- perabit opes, uerum etiam, quomodo recte has dispen sare ad Dei gloriam & sanctorum utilitatem deceat, edocebitur : significans nimirum hac ratione, eos E- uangelium Christi recepturos, sanctæq; Ecclesiæ Dei adiungendos. Cæterum quia hic aperte dicitur, uen- turos hostes à Kittim, id est Græcis, nonnulli censue- runt prophetam loqui de uastatione longe post factā per Alexandrum Macedonem, comitatum Græcorum exercitu, quo totam debellauit Asiam. Atqui magis pla- cet, accipere hæc omnia de uastatione Tyri facta per regem Babylonis Nebuchadnezzar, de qua fit mentio Ezechiel. 26. Nam & maximè consentaneum uero est, hunc regem Babylonicum circiter idem tempus, quo oppressit regnum Iudæ ac Ierusalem, subiugasse pari- ter & Tyrum haud procul disitam : præterea quam- diu durauit captiuitas populi Iudaici in Babylone, tam diu quoque Tyrum fuisse deiectam : rursus autem po- pulo illo restituto, hanc similiter coeptam restitui, id quod etiam ex Ezræ capite 3. confirmari utcun- que posset.
main_text.head: Vlulate naues Tharsis.) Propositio ad uici- nos insulares, ut doleant propter subuersam Tyrum, ad quam

page.notes: Page is printed in a single column with no marginal notes. The last line is partly obscured by a smudge at the right edge ("quam" partly visible, final letters faint). The "quam" word is ambiguous at the line end; I read it as "quam" with the final letters doubtful. The heading at the end is a line of commentary text rather than a true heading and may be better as a paragraph. The phrase "haud procul disitam" may be "disitam" for "disitam" as printed; left as printed. The word "Tyrum" in "ut doleant propter subuersam Tyrum" is clear. Running head and page number are read from the top of the page.
